Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
8 October 2026 .
Brent $ 103.92 + 3.17 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain, MarineLink, and Reuters report attack risks for tankers are rising as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes it has not authorized.

02 BBC News reports the tanker Acers was struck by multiple projectiles in the Gulf off Qatar, with casualties aboard; the attack occurred on October 7.

03 Brent crude stood at $103.92, up 3.17% over 24 hours, as of 21:25 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains a live hazard for commercial shipping, with gCaptain, MarineLink, and Reuters all reporting that attack risks for tankers are rising after Iran issued new warnings that it will block routes it has not authorized. That threat sits alongside an established pattern of strikes: BBC News reports the oil and chemical tanker Acers was hit by multiple projectiles in the Gulf off Qatar on October 7, with casualties aboard. The United States on Thursday imposed sanctions on 22 tankers and dozens of individuals and companies linked to Iran's oil trade, per gCaptain. Reuters and The Hindu report that Strait of Hormuz transits have fallen to their lowest level in over two months following the attacks. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent crude stood at $103.92, up 3.17% over 24 hours, as of 21:25 UTC; WTI stood at $91.18. On the policy front, gCaptain and BNN Bloomberg report that Iran has warned it will close routes it deems unauthorized, while US CENTCOM has separately maintained that transit lanes are open to vessels not violating the US blockade. Democracy Now! reports a tanker was struck north of Qatar after Iran warned ships against bypassing its blockade. The attacker has not been publicly identified by an independent authority in any of these incidents. The feed indexed 46 headlines in the last 24 hours. As of 21:20 UTC, 220 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
